claim_text: Closer-to-failure effort relates more clearly to hypertrophy than strength, with important uncertainty.

claim_text: Periodization may benefit 1RM strength more than hypertrophy when volume is equated.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Give strength mode more explicit intensity/skill periodization.

claim_text: RPE/RIR can regulate loading but relies on calibration.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Combine subjective effort with objective history.

claim_text: Volume has a graded relationship with hypertrophy, with individual diminishing returns.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Add volume conditionally, not as a fixed ladder for everyone.

claim_text: Exact MacroFactor load estimator, RP set coefficients and hidden scores are private.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Use versioned transparent analogues; never claim exact clone.

claim_text: Pain must be separate from fatigue and performance.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Pain state blocks automatic escalation and routes to review.
source_boundary_as_documented: Product safety design; not a diagnosis.

claim_text: MacroFactor custom programs default to 7 cycles, support 1–52 cycles and up to 14 unique training days per cycle.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Model repeating cycle templates separately from dated sessions.

claim_text: MacroFactor requires user-selected starting loads before sufficient exercise history exists.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Use a calibrated cold-start flow; do not fabricate precise loads.

claim_text: Equipment rounding, plate/bar inclusion and pin-loaded ranges materially constrain feasible recommendations.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Make rounding, fallback and warnings explicit in the recommendation object.

claim_text: MacroFactor public warm-up and rest defaults are execution aids, not working-set stimulus rules.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Store warm-ups separately; expose configurable rest defaults with readiness override.

claim_text: MacroFactor exposes exercise/muscle performance and export surfaces, but exact e1RM and weighting formulas are not public.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Version analytics separately from prescription formulas.

claim_text: Strength transfer is smaller when testing a movement different from the trained movement.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Keep exercise-specific strength histories and anchor lifts.

claim_text: More weekly set volume is associated with more strength and hypertrophy with diminishing returns.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Increase volume gradually and learn the individual response.

claim_text: Frequency is mainly a volume-distribution/practice variable for strength when volume is equated; hypertrophy evidence supports roughly two exposures more clearly than one.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Use two exposures as a practical prior, not a rule.

claim_text: RIR autoregulation can improve strength versus fixed percentage loading, but RIR accuracy is imperfect.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Use RIR with confidence, history and error bands.

claim_text: Deload practice is common at roughly 5–6 week intervals, but survey evidence does not establish a universal causal interval.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Support scheduled plus evidence-triggered deloads; do not hard-code a calendar superstition.

claim_text: A recent dose-response meta-analysis found the strongest relative evidence for fractional accounting of indirect sets.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Store direct and indirect sets separately; expose `1.0 direct + 0.5 indirect` only as a replaceable view.

claim_text: Concurrent training effects depend on sex, modality, duration, frequency and outcome; lower-body strength may be more sensitive than whole-muscle hypertrophy.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Track cardio context and repeated lower-body performance; do not impose a blanket cardio penalty.

claim_text: Velocity-loss thresholds can trade strength-oriented fatigue control against hypertrophy-oriented relative volume.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Support optional device-measured velocity loss as a feature-flagged signal; never infer it from reps.

claim_text: Problematic low energy availability/REDs is a complex clinical syndrome; no universal energy-availability cutoff diagnoses it.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Use a non-diagnostic fueling-safety review state and route to qualified care.

claim_text: Chest pain, collapse/fainting, severe breathing difficulty, neurological symptoms and suspected heat stroke are hard-stop concerns.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Enter `emergency_stop`; no training prescription or load adjustment.

claim_text: A boolean pain flag cannot represent acute illness, cardiopulmonary, neurological, heat, energy-availability and mental-health pathways.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Replace it with structured health events and a priority-ordered safety state machine.

claim_text: Return after illness/injury should be criteria-based, not cleared by elapsed days alone.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Require symptom resolution, functional tolerance and clinician clearance where appropriate.

claim_text: True individual response and measurement error require repeated, standardised observations; one short block cannot establish a non-response.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Add measurement-specific typical error/MDC and `unknown` response status.

claim_text: ACWR thresholds do not provide a reliable universal injury-risk prescription.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Do not implement an ACWR danger score; retain contextual load history only.

claim_text: Missing health data is not evidence of normal health, and wearable recovery scores cannot override red flags.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Use `insufficient_data`; safety state precedence beats readiness scores.

claim_text: MacroFactor separates repeating/completed program lifecycle actions and preserves workout history.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Model `repeat_block`, `complete_program`, `activate_program` and history preservation as events.

claim_text: MacroFactor backfill is manual and custom/altered programs can still use Smart Progression without automatically changing exercise selection.

claim_text: Program edits can cascade across RIR, sets and rep bounds; post-set RIR corrections feed future recommendations.
implementation_or_status_as_documented: Require transactional diff/commit and preserve original plus corrected observations.

claim_text: RIR can vary by set, and later-set rep reductions at constant RIR can be normal fatigue.

claim_text: Warm-up configuration is hierarchical and can be overridden at exercise/session level.

claim_text: Swapping an exercise starts a new future progression series, while historical context may remain visible.

claim_text: Exercises/workouts can be skipped for a cycle or temporarily and later restored.

claim_text: MacroFactor supersets are grouped rounds with rest after the round; RP manual adjacency is a distinct workflow.

claim_text: RP mesocycle length should vary with training age, and time limitation is different from recovery limitation.
